I guess I just never thought about it, though it makes sense because of the auto industry, but I never realized just how high Detroit's population was in 1950, especially compared to today.

It's kind of a clickbait title, although the article does describe the changes in population over that time, so the actual ratio of population to police isn't the highest in 100 years. Here's the breakdown:

1920: 1,108 people/officer

1930: 499 people/officer

1950: 521 people/officer

1970: 380 people/officer

1990: 310 people/officer

2000: 303 people/officer

2015: 452 people/officer

if they add 480 additional officers: 348 people/officer

People per officer probably isn't the best measure of how many police officers are really needed, but the overall number of officers is an even worse measure.
